title: AutoRE: Bayesian-Optimization-based Automatic Reliability Enhancement Tool for Flow-based Microfluidic Biochips
problem: Flow-based microfluidic biochips suffer from low yield due to manufacturing defects causing malfunctions; while reliability quantification models exist, automatic layout optimization to enhance reliability is lacking.
motivation: Manufacturing defects in microfluidic biochips reduce yield; systematic layout optimization can improve reliability without altering core topology.
method: AutoRE tests many different physical layouts of a microfluidic chip—adjusting component sizes and positions—while keeping the connections between parts the same. It uses Bayesian optimization (a search method that learns from each test to find good solutions efficiently) to explore these variations and identify the layout that works most reliably when manufactured.
key_novelty: It's the first automatic tool to make microfluidic biochips more reliable by exploring different physical layouts using Bayesian optimization (a search method that learns as it tests).
contributions: First automated reliability enhancement tool for microfluidic biochip layout optimization
Bayesian optimization-based search for reliable layout variants
Maintains topology while varying spatial parameters
Average reliability improvement of 40% across testcases
limitations: Limited to flow-based biochips; scalability to different chip types and practical manufacturing constraints not discussed.
primary_theme: Bayesian-optimized reliability enhancement for microfluidic biochips
